newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia stocks mostly higher, further gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Croatia stocks mostly higher, further gains seen.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly higher in brisk trade on Wednesday, with drugs concern Pliva accounting for two-thirds of the transactions and traders predicted mild growth would continue this week.
"Very active trade confirms that prices are generally going to rise in the short term, although without major changes," Zoran Ilic of Consult Invest brokerage said.
Seven of 13 active issues rose, two fell and four were flat. Both volume and turnover fell slightly to 20,919 units and 13.3 million kuna on Tuesday.
Fully listed Pliva was the most active stock, rising 15 kuna to 495 kuna on volume of 14,107 shares.
"Pliva took the spotlight, perhaps mostly because of rumours that it is about to take over a factory in Poland," analyst Denis Fuduric of Invesment Bank Austria told Reuters.
He said the company's imminent opening of a new azithromycin plant had already begun to attract foreign buyers.
But another broker said the price would move up only after the annual shareholders' meeting due in two days, backed by the prospect of good results.

Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka was stable at 2,035 kuna on volume of 2,143 shares and traders said its price would rise in the medium term as soon as it absorbs the 400 million German marks raised through a foreign syndicated loan.
Chocolate maker Kras was the day's leading gainer. It added 23 kuna to 440 with 1,188 shares sold and was seen stabilising after a 10 percent rise in the past three days.
Another popular food stock Podravka inched down three kuna to 285 on a decraeased volume of 1,375 after Tuesday's 4,163 units and was expected to stabilise.
Blue chip Varazdinska Banka fell most, losing seven kuna or 3.3 percent to 207 with 676 shares sold.
Two of three active hoteliers rose and one was flat. Traders cited Jadranturist as a possible short-term gainer while the others were not expected to move up before the autumn.
